data.description:
## Incident Overview

### Expected Behavior
When merge-to-main.sh runs in PR mode (`dso.workflow=ci-pr`), it should fetch and rebase/merge the destination branch (origin/main) into the session branch BEFORE creating the PR. This ensures:
- The PR diff is minimal (just the session changes vs current main)
- No stale base causes merge conflicts at PR-merge time
- Reviewers see only relevant changes, not catch-up noise

### Actual Behavior
Observed during the 2026-05-17 batch fix session: merge-to-main-pr.sh pushed and created PRs on `worktree-20260516-164045` against `main` without first fast-forwarding the session branch to origin/main. Each successive PR's diff included only my new commit, but the underlying branch fell behind whenever main advanced via concurrent merges. The first push after a PR merge often failed with non-fast-forward and required `_fetch_and_rebase_branch` retry — a working but lossy recovery.

The pre-push step already calls `_fetch_and_rebase_branch` as a retry guard (plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh:512). That's the right code path, but it fires AFTER the push fails, not BEFORE the PR is constructed. So:
- PR titles and body are derived from a non-updated diff
- If the rebase has merge complications, the script reaches the PR-create step with an inconsistent worktree
- The first push attempt always wastes a network round-trip when origin/main has advanced

### Suggested Fix
At the start of merge-to-main-pr.sh's PR-create phase (before _derive_pr_title), unconditionally:
1. `git fetch origin main`
2. `git rebase origin/main` or `git merge --no-edit origin/main` (whichever matches project policy)
3. Bail with a clear error if conflicts arise

This pre-sync replaces the current 'push, fail, fetch+rebase, retry' pattern with 'fetch+rebase, then push' — same outcome, fewer wasted round-trips, cleaner PR diff.

### Skills and Workflows
- Script: plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh (PR mode entry point)
- Affected lines: 505-523 (publish branch) and earlier (PR construction)
- Called from: .claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh wrapper
data.title: [merge-to-main]: PR-mode skips destination-branch sync before creating PR -> stale base produces unnecessary conflicts and review noise
